summary: Iteration 46 — Alignment Milestones. Verified backend milestone-crossing detection on snapshot insert, timeline exposure of latest_snapshot_id + latest_milestones, and the AlignmentMilestoneCelebration UI (highest-milestone rendering, 24 confetti particles, share button, dismiss + localStorage persistence across reload). 17/17 new iter46 backend tests pass; 51/52 regression (iter42-45) still pass (1 pre-existing skip). Frontend flow verified end-to-end at /special-needs-v2/educational-deep-dive/compare/{share_id} with a seeded 98% aligned share that crossed [50,75,90] on the very first snapshot — the UI correctly picks 90 (highest) and shows the gold 9-in-10 copy.
critical_code_review_comments: Milestone-detection reads the PRIOR snapshot with `sort=[('created_at', -1)]` BEFORE inserting the new one — that ordering is correct, but if two comparison views race for the same share in the same millisecond (unlikely but possible on shared servers), both could compute the same prior_pct and both could stamp milestones. Consider a unique index on (share_id, snapshot_key) plus catching DuplicateKeyError to make the insert idempotent. Today the dedupe relies on the app-level find_one which is racy.

`current_pct = int((comparison.get('summary') or {}).get('aligned_pct') or 0)` will silently coerce a float to int (floor). Fine today because build_comparison rounds already, but if that ever changes a 74.9 would be counted as 74 and miss the 75 threshold. Prefer `float(...)` comparison, or lock in rounding at the source with a doc comment.

`milestones_crossed` is stored as a plain list on the snapshot row but the model isn't typed — no Pydantic schema pins that shape. A future refactor that renames the key would break the timeline endpoint silently. A tiny TypedDict / Pydantic model for the snapshot doc would prevent this.

Frontend AlignmentMilestoneCelebration re-reads localStorage in a useEffect right after initial mount — this can cause a brief render of the celebration before it flips to dismissed on next paint. In practice the initial useState already reads localStorage so this is a duplicate check; consider removing the effect to avoid a flash on slow devices.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (celebration renders, highest milestone selected, confetti=24, dismiss + localStorage persistence across reload verified)

seed_data_creation: Backend tests seed edu/psych/med_deep_assessments with identical answers for parent1/parent2 (yielding ~96-98% aligned) and rewrite the most recent snapshot's summary.aligned_pct via Mongo to exercise the prior→current milestone-crossing branches. All test-created shares are revoked and deep_dive_compare_snapshots rows are deleted in the module-scope autouse teardown. UI verification: a temporary edu-deep share (edu_deep_share_a195085be2e4) with milestones [50,75,90] was seeded via /tmp/seed_iter46.py and revoked after testing.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter46 verified. The milestone-detection logic uses the PRIOR snapshot's summary.aligned_pct (or 0 for the first snapshot ever). To test specific crossings deterministically, seed identical answers for both parents (yields >=95% aligned), then rewrite the latest snapshot's summary.aligned_pct in Mongo and bump the assessment's updated_at (the API re-stamps it on every write) — the next GET /compare/{share_id} will insert a fresh snapshot with milestones computed against the rewritten prior. The UI picks Math.max(latest_milestones) so a snapshot crossing multiple thresholds only shows the highest tier's copy. Confetti = 24 CSS particles inside {prefix}-confetti; dismissal persists under localStorage key `sacop.milestone_dismissed.{snapshot_id}`.
